question: Can I use the LCH hi-limit (00-414146-00002) instead of the LC117 (00-419670-00001)?
short_answer: No. They are both 450F-class fryer hi-limits, but one is auto-reset and the other is manual-reset, and the set points differ (450 F vs 435 F). Substituting one for the other changes the safety behaviour of the fryer.

question: Can I use the two-lead thermopile (00-410839-00004) instead of the coaxial one (00-348358-00001)?
short_answer: No. Both are 36 in, 250-750 mV thermopiles, and that is exactly why they get confused. The 00-348358-00001 is the coaxial type with a 3/8-32 thread; 00-410839-00004 is the two-lead type with a different terminal arrangement. Same length and same output voltage do not make them interchangeable.

question: Can I replace 00-419670-00001 with 00-410840-00002?
short_answer: Usually yes, but check the sensing bulb first. The successor 00-410840-00002 uses a 1/4 in x 4-1/2 in bulb, while the original LC117 uses a 1/4 in x 4-7/8 in bulb - about 3/8 in shorter. Both are 450 F auto-reset hi-limits with a 30 in capillary and a 3/8 in MPT stuffing box.

question: Is 00-913153 the same part as 00-411506-00013?
short_answer: Distributor interchange tables treat 00-913153 as the current number for the same RX thermostat kit. This is a distributor-level cross-reference, not a statement published by the manufacturer, so verify against your own parts manual before ordering.

question: Is the non-OEM version of 00-348361-00001 the same as the Hobart-branded one?
short_answer: Possibly - and that is the point. Fenwal builds this thermostat; Hobart resells it under its own number. On this part, OEM and non-OEM listings often describe the same device sold through different channels. The price gap can be several times, so ask the seller whether the body carries the Fenwal name and a UL file number before paying the OEM premium.

question: Are RTCU700609 and RTBF800164 the same thermostat?
short_answer: No. RTCU700609 is the electronic regulating thermostat (105-185 C) for Hobart HEF-series fryers. RTBF800164 is the separate high-limit thermostat. They do different jobs and are not substitutes for each other.

question: Can I use the 24 V electronic-ignition gas valve (00-410841-00028) in place of a millivolt valve (00-410841-00001)?
short_answer: No. A millivolt valve is operated by a thermopile (750 mV open circuit, about 500 mV under load) through a bleed-gas safety valve. The 24 V electronic-ignition valve has a different operator and is wired to an ignition module. They are not interchangeable, and the ignition module and valve are a matched pair.

question: Can I use an 8500 W element in place of a 5500 W element?
short_answer: No. Element wattage, voltage and physical length must all match the original. Fitting a higher-wattage element increases current draw beyond the contactor and wiring rating; fitting the wrong voltage delivers the wrong wattage even at the same nominal size.

question: Can I use the natural-gas valve (00-410841-00001) on LP?
short_answer: No, not without the LP conversion kit. The LP version (00-410841-00002) uses the same body with LP conversion kit 51-1470. A natural-gas valve running on LP will not regulate correctly and is a safety hazard.

question: What is the difference between the RX, KX and K fryer thermostats?
short_answer: They are three different thermostat families with different bulb diameters, capillary lengths and temperature ranges. RX is the 24 in, 200-400 F regulating kit. KX uses a 1/4 in bulb with a 12-1/8 in capillary. K is a separate family again. The letter matters more than the shape.
